summary: Admit WooCommerce as a bidirectional storefront provider and add reusable typed commerce write/return/webhook SDK-v1 surfaces without changing frozen Connector/Runtime roots.

impacts.evidence: WooCommerce account configuration and mappings remain organization/workspace scoped; no tenant selector enters provider payloads.
Order projection intentionally excludes Woo billing/shipping/customer identity fields; credentials remain behind SecretAccessor.
No public TORGNEXA REST operation changes; Connector SDK changes are additive typed interfaces only.
No canonical event schema changes; Woo webhooks enter existing inbox/sync boundaries after verification.
Frozen Connector/Runtime roots are unchanged; commerce write, return and webhook interfaces are additive SDK-v1 capability surfaces.
No database schema migration is required; Task-010 mappings and existing inbox/reconciliation persistence remain authoritative.
Store host/base path are constrained, query-string credentials are forbidden, webhook HMAC is constant-time verified and ambiguous writes fail closed.
Host Task-017/082 policy remains mandatory before invoking commerce writes; provider capability does not bypass approvals/compliance.
Write receipts and reconciliation outcomes preserve remote IDs for existing audit/lineage orchestration without storing raw credentials.
SKU reconciliation protects creates; exact-state writes use read-before/read-after reconciliation; webhook replay uses signed-material identity.
Woo inbound webhooks require expected-topic binding and verified HMAC; provider outbound requests use only configured HTTPS store host.
Provider errors/rate-limit health are normalized through existing Connector SDK SLO surfaces.
Connector admission is additive and can be disabled per account; no schema rollback is required.
Deterministic unit tests and the Task-064 13-check provider report are required and recorded.
